rationale: The assistant told the customer to unplug first and correctly led with the filter and spray-arm checks, which matched the hidden cause and got the blockage cleared. However, it pivoted to asking for a model number and surfaced a 'check a suitable replacement' panel after a single 'stiff' report and before the arm had even been cleaned, which was premature, and its final summary attributed the fault 'almost probably' to the upper arm while ignoring the filter that was 'full of food n grease'. It never asked about the programme, salt or rinse aid, so the aggravating factors (quick 30-minute wash, never filled salt, limescale) went unaddressed, and it did not ask for a confirmatory test wash. A reasonable, mostly resolved outcome but with gaps in the maintenance advice and a slightly part-sales-leaning turn.
